decisions.reason: As a newly launched software line that is very close to the core practice-management offer and the firm's digital healthcare direction, it still has option value and is unlikely to be withdrawn so early without negative evidence.

The education institute fits the firm's training and customer-support capabilities, but as a somewhat less core and potentially more resource-intensive service than software, it has a higher withdrawal risk while management still learns its value.

A remote screen-sharing support tool is closely tied to the installed software base, likely cheap to maintain relative to its customer-service value, and therefore worth keeping while demand and use become clearer.
